newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine president picks new agriculture minister.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine president picks new agriculture minister.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma has appointed Deputy Prime Minister Mykhailo Zubets as Ukraine's new agriculture minister, the presidential press service said. Zubets was already responsible for the farm sector.

"Mykhailo Zubets will remain deputy prime minister and will take on his new responsibilities," a spokesman said. The troubled agriculture sector has been without a permanent minister since the last minister was sacked in February.
Ukraine has forecast a 38 million tonne grain harvest this year compared to a poor 25.4 million tonnes in 1996 after a severe drought at the start of the growing season.

Kuchma fired minister Anatoly Khorishko to try to reverse the declining fortunes of the agriculture sector, beset by shortages of fertilisers, herbicides, fuel, and money, which began after independence in 1991.
Spring sowing of the grain harvest has started in many regions of Ukraine.
